args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft → Lender-Required Form)

Document: Account Control Agreement (Counterparty Paper Review)
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Parties (as defined herein): Secured Party / Lender; Debtor / Grantor; Depository Bank
Status: Markup incorporating all required modifications and insertions
Legend: [DELETE: text to be deleted]  [INSERT: text to be inserted]  [COMMENT: drafting note]

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SOURCE CONTROLS APPLIED
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Internal ACA / deposit-account collateral playbook (firm standard positions).
2. Executed Credit Agreement (Secured Obligations; collateral and control requirements).
3. Depository Bank standard form Account Control Agreement (UCC § 9-104 control mechanics).
4. Account details / account identification schedule.
5. Deal correspondence (controlling instruction): client will CONCEDE basket conversion (deductible → tipping); any SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION is a WALK-AWAY issue.
6. Schedules and Exhibits: Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities); Exhibit B (survival matrix) — scheduled exceptions CONTROL over general base statements.
7. Counterparty markup deviations identified and addressed below.

Distractor administrative correspondence (unrelated engagement) is disregarded.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [●], 20[●] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and among:

(i) [DEBTOR LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Debtor");
(ii) [SECURED PARTY / ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT LEGAL NAME], as [Administrative Agent / Collateral Agent] for the benefit of the Secured Parties (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns, the "Secured Party"); and
(iii) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

A. Debtor and Secured Party are parties to that certain [Credit Agreement][Security Agreement], dated as of [●] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), pursuant to which Debtor has granted to Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Account (as defined below) and all cash, funds, financial assets, instruments, securities entitlements and other property from time to time credited thereto (collectively, the "Account Collateral").

B. Bank maintains the Deposit Account for Debtor.

C. The parties enter into this Agreement to perfect Secured Party's security interest in the Account Collateral by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), including UCC § 9-104, and to set forth the rights and obligations of the parties with respect to the Deposit Account.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

TO:      Deal Team / Partner
FROM:    Contracts / Banking Counsel
RE:      Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviations, Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms, and Recommended Positions
MATTER:  Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
DATE:    [Engagement Date]

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA" or "Counterparty Draft") against (i) the firm's internal ACA / deposit-account collateral playbook, (ii) the executed Credit Agreement (including collateral, cash-dominion, and indemnity constructs), (iii) the depository bank's standard form ACA, (iv) the account details package, and (v) related correspondence and checklists. Schedules and exhibits were reconciled concurrently: Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), and Exhibit B (survival matrix). Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.

Controlling deal-team instruction (latest partner email — supersedes earlier contrary priority ordering):
• Client WILL CONCEDE conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
• Any reduction of survival periods for core representations is a WALK-AWAY issue.

Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in the matter folder was disregarded.

Bottom line: The Counterparty Draft is not acceptable as presented. It silently erodes indemnity economics, introduces MAE regulatory carve-outs that collide with Schedule 3.7 disclosures, shortens survival in direct conflict with Exhibit B, and omits market-standard UCC control, NOEC, subordination, and bank-form override protections required for a perfected, first-priority deposit-account lien. We have prepared a full tracked-changes redline (aca-redline.docx) implementing all required deletions and insertions. Survival restoration is non-negotiable. Basket tipping is conceded. Indemnity cap restoration, MAE fix, Schedule 5.2 anti-shift language, and full control package are high-priority required positions.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SCOPE OF REVIEW AND SOURCE HIERARCHY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Sources reviewed and hierarchy applied:
1. Controlling deal correspondence (latest partner instruction on basket concession vs. survival walk-away).
2. Exhibit B Survival Matrix; Schedule 3.7; Schedule 5.2 (control over general base statements).
3. Executed Credit Agreement (Secured Obligations definition; collateral and control conditions; cash management / dominion; indemnity architecture).
4. Internal playbook — Account Control Agreements / deposit-account perfection by control (UCC §§ 9-104, 9-314, 9-327, 9-340).
5. Depository bank standard form ACA (operational baseline; must yield to Secured Party protective terms on control, priority, NOEC, indemnity, survival, termination).
6. Account details / identification checklist (Schedule A integrity; successor accounts; notice contacts for NOEC).
7. Counterparty markup deviations list.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference (Counterparty Draft): Article VI (Indemnification), cap provision.
Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement: Debtor indemnity for control-agreement and collateral matters should run to the full Secured Obligations (principal plus interest, fees, enforcement costs), with no cap below outstanding Obligations; fundamental reps, fraud, willful misconduct, and collateral-diversion claims uncapped. Cap must not undercut Credit Agreement indemnity floor.
Deviation: Counterparty silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap below firm-standard / Credit Agreement levels without call-out in a issues list.
Risk rating: HIGH
Exposure analysis: A reduced cap caps recovery for Bank or Secured Party losses arising from adverse claims to the Deposit Account, conflicting control assertions, operational errors Debtor caused, or third-party claims. In a downside scenario involving Account Collateral equal to a material portion of facility size, the reduced cap creates uninsured shortfall risk and weakens the economic deterrent against Debtor impairment of control. Interaction with Schedule 5.2: if the reduced cap is read to limit claims connected to retained liabilities, Secured Party could absorb exposure the Credit Agreement allocated to Debtor.
Recommended position: REJECT reduction. Restore cap to the greater of outstanding Obligations and playbook/Credit Agreement floor. Carve out from any cap: (i) fraud/willful misconduct, (ii) fundamental representations (authority, ownership, no conflicting control), (iii) diversion/impairment of Account Collateral or control, and (iv) Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 6.2, 6.4, 4.5.
Negotiation posture: Required. Not within client concession.

ISSUE 2 — Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Article VI (Indemnification), basket provision.
Playbook requirement: Prefer deductible basket (Debtor bears losses only above threshold, and only the excess). Tipping basket (once threshold exceeded, liability from dollar one) is more favorable to the indemnified party and more burdensome to Debtor.
Deviation: Counterparty converts deductible → tipping basket.
Risk rating: MODERATE (process) / LOW-MODERATE (substantive for Secured Party)
Exposure analysis: Tipping basket increases Debtor's potential liability once the threshold is crossed (first-dollar true-up). For Secured Party this is economically better than a deductible; the "risk" is primarily commercial/relationship and consistency with other Loan Document indemnity constructs, not secured-party shortfall.
Recommended position: CONCEDE, per controlling deal correspondence. Accept tipping basket at the Credit Agreement dollar threshold; document expressly that this is the sole conceded indemnity-economics point and that no further erosion (especially cap reduction) is accepted. Implemented in aca-redline.docx § 6.3.
Negotiation posture: Client concession — accept.

ISSUE 3 — Material Adverse Effect Definition — Regulatory Carve-Outs
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Definitions (MAE); related Debtor representations; default/termination triggers cross-walking to Credit Agreement MAE usage where incorporated.
Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement: MAE must protect Secured Party against material adverse changes affecting Debtor's ability to perform, enforceability, and collateral. Regulatory actions that are the very risk profile of the credit should not be freely carved out, particularly where disclosure schedules identify live regulatory inquiries.
Deviation: Counterparty adds carve-outs for regulatory action/inquiry/investigation/examination and related regulatory changes — "exactly the kind at issue in this matter."
Schedule interaction (CONTROLLING): Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. If carve-outs stand, Debtor could argue that adverse developments in those inquiries cannot constitute MAE or support MAE-based remedies, gutting the disclosure's risk-allocation purpose. Scheduled exceptions control over general base language; the deliverable must not allow markup carve-outs to override Schedule 3.7.
Risk rating: HIGH
Exposure analysis: With two pending inquiries already disclosed, a regulatory carve-out creates a roadmap for Debtor to neutralize MAE and related representation bring-downs precisely when regulatory risk crystallizes. That undermines pricing, covenant package, and control-agreement default triggers tied to Credit Agreement Events of Default. Could also impair Secured Party's ability to exercise dominion or NOEC in a regulatory stress scenario if Debtor contests the predicate default.
Recommended position: REJECT regulatory free-pass carve-outs. Redefine MAE without excluding regulatory actions; state expressly that Schedule 3.7 disclosures do not qualify MAE or excuse defaults/indemnity under the ACA or Credit Agreement; at most, allow a narrow disproportionate-impact qualifier for industry-wide regulatory changes that do not disproportionately affect Debtor and do not affect Account Collateral, control, or Lien priority. Require prompt notice of Schedule 3.7 developments (covenant). Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 1.1 (MAE), 3.2(c), 4.3.
Negotiation posture: Required. Not conceded.

ISSUE 4 — Shortened Survival / Limitation Period for Core Representations
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Article VII (Survival); Counterparty new limitation period.
Playbook / Credit Agreement / Exhibit B requirement: Survival of core collateral, ownership, authority, and control representations must match Exhibit B Survival Matrix and Credit Agreement collateral-rep survival; fundamental reps typically survive indefinitely or for SOL-equivalent periods; indemnities survive through applicable statute of limitations plus a short tail. Exhibit B controls over conflicting general statements.
Deviation: Counterparty inserts a new limitation period that shortens survival for core representations below Exhibit B.
Schedule interaction (CONTROLLING): Exhibit B sets the survival matrix the markup contradicts. Exhibit B wins.
Deal correspondence (CONTROLLING): Survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier emails stating opposite priority are superseded.
Risk rating: CRITICAL (WALK-AWAY)
Exposure analysis: Short survival extinguishes Secured Party claims for misrepresentation as to ownership of Account Collateral, absence of conflicting control agreements, authority, and Schedule A accuracy after an artificially early date — often before latent third-party claims or Bank operational issues surface. In enforcement or bankruptcy, expired survival can bar indemnity and rep-based remedies essential to defending priority and control. Given Exhibit B and partner instruction, accepting this term would violate client mandate.
Recommended position: REJECT IN FULL. Restore Exhibit B periods; indefinite survival for fundamental reps (authority, enforceability, ownership, no conflicting control, Schedule A accuracy); indemnity survival through SOL + 60 days (and through final resolution of timely asserted claims); tolling during stays. State expressly that any shortened limitation period is deleted and Exhibit B controls. Implemented in aca-redline.docx Article VII.
Negotiation posture: WALK-AWAY. Non-concedable.

ISSUE 5 — Missing UCC § 9-104 Control Package / NOEC Mechanics
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Counterparty Draft control provisions (incomplete relative to bank form + playbook).
Playbook / Bank form / Credit Agreement requirement: Express Bank agreement to comply with Secured Party instructions without Debtor consent (UCC § 9-104(a)(2)); clear Notice of Exclusive Control mechanics; post-NOEC freeze and confirmation; automatic coverage of successor/renumbered accounts; acknowledgment of "control" for perfection (§§ 9-104, 9-314); priority vs. other secured parties (§ 9-327); treatment of Bank setoff (§ 9-340) after control.
Deviation / gap: Counterparty paper omits or weakens critical control elements standard in depository-bank ACAs and required by Credit Agreement conditions precedent to relying on deposit-account collateral.
Risk rating: HIGH (perfection / priority / enforceability)
Exposure analysis: Incomplete control language risks failure of perfection by control, weaker priority against subsequent control parties or Bank, delays or disputes in exercising dominion upon default, and CP failure under the Credit Agreement if counsel cannot give a clean control opinion or checklist sign-off.
Recommended position: INSERT full control package: Secured Party instruction primacy; NOEC form (Exhibit C); one-Business-Day confirmation; successor-account automatic coverage; express UCC control acknowledgment; exclusivity covenant (no other control agreements). Implemented in aca-redline.docx Article II, § 9.8, Exhibit C.
Negotiation posture: Required for closing / CP satisfaction.

ISSUE 6 — Bank Setoff, Banker's Lien, and Subordination Underspecified or Overbroad
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Bank rights / account agreement incorporation; setoff provisions.
Playbook / Bank form (as modified for lenders): Bank may retain limited rights for customary fees and returned items; all other setoff/banker's liens subordinated to Secured Party; post-NOEC setoff tightly limited.
Deviation / gap: Counterparty draft leaves Bank setoff unrestricted or defers entirely to Account Agreement, which typically favors Bank and can prime or erode Account Collateral after default.
Risk rating: HIGH
Exposure analysis: Unrestricted setoff can drain the Deposit Account after default or upon NOEC, defeating cash collateral. In insolvency, unclear subordination complicates § 9-340 analysis and recovery.
Recommended position: Express subordination of Bank claims other than customary fees and pre-NOEC returned items; post-NOEC setoff freeze except narrow returned-item window; Secured Party priority acknowledgment. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 2.3, 5.3.
Negotiation posture: Required. Bank will negotiate returned-item mechanics; substance non-negotiable.

ISSUE 7 — Silent Shift Risk on Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities via Indemnity Markup
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Article VI interacting with Schedule 5.2; Counterparty cap/basket changes.
Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement: Retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 stay with Debtor; Loan Document amendments must not reallocate them to Secured Party.
Deviation: Cap reduction and basket restructuring, read together with general indemnity limitations, could silently shift or economically dilute Debtor responsibility for Schedule 5.2 items when claims intersect Account Collateral or ACA operations.
Risk rating: HIGH
Exposure analysis: If retained liabilities generate third-party claims against the Deposit Account or Bank, a reduced cap or poorly drafted basket may leave Secured Party bearing residual loss contrary to the negotiated risk allocation in the Credit Agreement schedules.
Recommended position: INSERT anti-shift provisions: Schedule 5.2 liabilities remain Debtor's; uncapped; not offsettable against Indemnified Person claims; no amendment to ACA indemnity alters Schedule 5.2 allocation. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 4.5, 6.2, 6.4.
Negotiation posture: Required.

ISSUE 8 — Termination Rights Too Permissive to Debtor; Release of Control Premature
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Termination article.
Playbook / Credit Agreement requirement: ACA terminates only on Secured Party written release, mutual agreement, or payment in full of Secured Obligations (other than unasserted contingent indemnity) plus commitment termination and Secured Party termination notice to Bank. No Debtor unilateral termination while Obligations outstanding.
Deviation / gap: Counterparty draft permits Debtor-driven termination on notice, risking loss of control while facility remains outstanding.
Risk rating: HIGH
Exposure analysis: Premature termination destroys perfection by control and can create an Event of Default under Credit Agreement collateral maintenance covenants, with potential unperfected period.
Recommended position: Delete Debtor unilateral termination; tie termination to Secured Party notice and Payment in Full mechanics. Implemented in aca-redline.docx § 8.1.
Negotiation posture: Required.

ISSUE 9 — Bank Standard Form / Account Agreement Override Missing
────────────────────────────────────────────
Section reference: Entire agreement / conflict provisions.
Playbook requirement: ACA controls over Bank standard form and Account Agreement as to Secured Party rights, control, priority, NOEC, Secured Party indemnity, and termination. Order of precedence documented.
Deviation / gap: Counterparty draft fails to lock precedence, leaving Bank's preprinted terms to undermine negotiated lender protections.
Risk rating: MODERATE-HIGH
Exposure analysis: Operational disputes default to Bank paper; NOEC timing, liability caps favoring Bank, or broad exculpation could impair enforcement.
Recommended position: Insert order of precedence: (1) ACA, (2) Credit Agreement (as between Debtor and Secured Party), (3) Bank form/Account Agreement. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 3.3(c), 5.2, 9.5.
Negotiation posture: Required; standard in negotiated bank ACAs.

Risk rating: MODERATE

Recommended position: Insert Schedule A integrity covenant, 3-Business-Day notice, automatic successor coverage. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§ 2.1, 2.6, Schedule A.
Negotiation posture: Required checklist item.

Risk rating: MODERATE

Recommended position: Insert targeted Bank indemnity for NOEC/exclusivity failures. Implemented in aca-redline.docx § 6.5.
Negotiation posture: Strong ask; often accepted in modified form by money-center banks.

Negotiation posture: Required for facilities with springing dominion.
